correctness.rationale: For normalized positive-definite nonnegative weak complement h on G=F_2^3, (A-A)∩ supp(h)={0}. A with |A|>=5 has A-A=G and hence h=delta_0, contradicting 1_A*h=1_G unless A=G. For |A|=3, A translates to {0,a,b}, S=A-A=span(a,b), h vanishes on S\{0}, sum_G h=8/3, and the nontrivial character with kernel S has Fourier coefficient 1-(8/3-1)=-2/3, violating positivity. Every size 1,2,4,8 subset has explicit tiling complement: 4 points either a plane or {0,a,b,c} for a basis, with complement {0,a+b+c}. A translational complement B yields h=1_B*1_-B/|B|, meeting all four conditions. Independently enumerated all 255 nonempty subsets: all 8+28+70+1 of sizes 1,2,4,8 tile and no others; analytic argument covers all.

originality.rationale: A separate published Resultary theorem (same 2026-10-04 release) proves that ANY normalized nonnegative weak tile of F_2^4 is a translational tile, without the stronger Fourier-positivity assumption. This implies the ENTIRE pd-flatness conclusion for F_2^3 by a simple cylinder lift: from weak h on A subset F_2^3 construct A× F_2 subset F_2^4 and h⊗ delta_0; this meets the F_2^4 theorem, so A× F_2 tiles and projection of any tiling complement supplies a tiling complement of A in F_2^3. Then |A| divides 8; every size 1,2,4,8 set tiles by the elementary constructions here. A subsequent published all-abelian-order-16 theorem independently reinforces broader coverage. These are mathematically dominating implications even without a verbatim F_2^3 table, so this original claim is covered.
